lesson_title: What If All the Money Vanished Tonight?
hook_text: Tomorrow morning every coin, note and bank card is gone. How do you buy breakfast?
clip_script: You wake up and the money is gone. You want bread. You offer a pencil. The shopkeeper has pencils. No deal. The taxi driver wants petrol, not pencils. Welcome to life without money. Now go back a few hundred years. In a village, families grew maize, herded cattle and built their own homes. Cattle were their savings, and they swapped only now and then. That was a traditional, self-sufficient society. Today your family buys almost everything, from bread to data, made by thousands of strangers. That is specialisation, and it only works because everyone accepts money. More specialising means more trading, and more trading means you need money.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen: a village with a kraal and fields on the left, a city street with a spaza shop and taxi on the right, and a disappearing coin in the middle.
mood: Playful and curious, a what-if story that turns into a big idea.
pacing: A quick bad-dream opening, then a calm left-right comparison.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list five things your family buys that it could never make itself.
